summary:
Sud contains Campania and Puglia, two of the six highest-victim regions in the 2012–2025 region-by-region study of anti-LGBT violence, and multiple documented public-space incidents directly relevant to a traveller: in Scampia (Naples), March 2025, two young men on a scooter stopped, insulted and assaulted a young man with homophobic slurs — part of an international rights federation's finding of a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence in 2024, with incidents reported almost monthly; and at the Torre Annunziata railway station (Campania), 13 October 2025, an activist and president of a local LGBT association was subjected to a verbal attack culminating in threats of stabbing by two young men — a public-transit setting any visitor could encounter. In Reggio Calabria (28 May 2024) a person was kidnapped, subjected to violence and robbed in the city centre; the police's swift intervention drew public commendation from Arcigay alongside demands for an anti-homophobia law.

Taranto (Puglia) and Termoli (Molise) featured in the 2025 national Pride circuit, indicating continued public LGBTQ presence in the south. No special-statute region in Sud used expanded competence against transgender people, and no criminal facility bans or enforcement mechanisms target visitors. The violence is criminal and street-level, not state-imposed — but its concentration and public-transit exposure raise the probability of encounter for a traveller.

sources.summary: LGBT Christian association's region-by-region analysis of homophobia incidents in Italy 2012–2025: identifies the six highest-victim regions, including Campania and Puglia (the southern pairing), and publishes the per-region incident table used to locate bias violence geographically.

International LGBT federation's annual country review for Italy (February 2025): finds a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence against LGBTI people in 2024, incidents reported almost monthly, including the March 2025 scooter-mounted assault of a young man in Scampia (Naples).

tangentialFactors: Every documented Sud incident in the record targeted gay men rather than trans people specifically; a visitor-facing pattern of public-space homophobia that trans-presenting travellers share without being separately named.
